goal: Make every copy, mirror, or move command a durable job whose single run ID follows every session and participating daemon and whose per-machine logs can be listed and read locally or remotely.
recommended_approach: Generate the run ID once at command start, propagate a typed RunTag through every session and delegation request, feed a shared blit-core RunLog adapter from bounded progress lanes, persist crash-safe retained JSONL logs per participant, role, and attempt, and expose symmetric local and daemon jobs commands while explicitly modeling simulated or discarded transfers.
comparison: The central architecture is sound: the run-ID guard passed, failed when SessionOpen.run_id forwarding was temporarily removed, and passed again after restoration; all seven existing job-log CLI tests pass. However, the local adapter lacks an execution disposition, so dry-run and null-sink activity can be recorded as real copies. A focused dry-run guard reproduced this at head and passed with a temporary suppression and zero-count fix; the worktree was restored to the reviewed SHA.
material_changes: Add truthful dry-run and null-sink log semantics, including explicit planned/discarded events or suppressed copied events and counts, complete option recording, and regression coverage for both modes.

findings.title: Simulated local transfers are recorded as real copies
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:166 — every local transfer attaches the audit lane; crates/blit-core/src/run_log.rs:280 maps every FileComplete to FileCopied; crates/blit-cli/src/run_log.rs:253 reports copied_files unchanged, while crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:3304 also counts null-sink payloads as written.
findings.predicted_failure: A successful `blit copy --dry-run` leaves the destination untouched but `blit jobs log` reports `copied planned.txt` and `summary 1 copied`; `--null` similarly claims copies while discarding writes and is not identified in the recorded options.
findings.better_approach: Thread a real/dry-run/null-sink disposition into RunLog, emit compatible planned or discarded events—or suppress copied events and counts—for non-real runs, record the disposition in RunInfo, and test that untouched destinations never produce copied claims.
